front.title: Considerations for Detecting Look-Alike Sender Identities in Platform Messaging

abstract.t: Users of consumer platforms -- job boards, marketplaces, education and early-career services -- receive messages from other parties inside the platform, where no enterprise mail gateway inspects them. Attackers impersonate the platform's own brand and support staff, and pose as recruiters or counterparties, using look-alike domains and display names. This document describes considerations for detecting look-alike sender identities at the level of the individual message and its sender, rather than at the domain-registration level. It records two concrete pitfalls observed in deployed libraries: Unicode confusable "skeleton" equality alone does not catch all mixed-script look-alikes, and several input validators accept host names containing invisible format characters. This document is informational and specifies no protocol.
